run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T06:26:06Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for frontend-proxy is explained by HTTP 504s that frontend-proxy returns on `/api/checkout` traffic: its own ingress spans record error=true, http.status_code=504 at a duration of ~15.0 s (a fixed upstream timeout), and a whole trace shows the request behind that 504 spending its time in frontend -> checkout `PlaceOrder` -> checkout `orders publish` (Kafka produce) at ~15.6-15.7 s. Checkout's Kafka produce latency was sub-millisecond (120-530 us) through 06:23:39 and became 11-17 s afterwards. The only change observed at that boundary is the kafka Deployment rollout at 06:23:35 (pod template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt), which replaced the single broker (old pod killed 06:23:37, replacement serving only from ~06:25:16). During that gap checkout got `connection refused` to the kafka Service ClusterIP 100.65.62.181:9092 and `circuit breaker is open`; slow 504-producing ingress spans first appear in the 5-minute window ending 06:25 and the alert fired at 06:26:06. Kafka is not CPU-bound, endpoint-less or network-isolated now, and the ~11-17 s produce latency that keeps every PlaceOrder above the proxy timeout persists without a broker-side error, so the exact reason that latency stays high and who issued the 06:23:35 rollout remain unproven. The fault-injection flag `kafkaQueueProblems` (defaultVariant on, in ConfigMap flagd-config) remains a candidate but does not by itself explain the onset: its declared consumer-side delay is not visible in accounting spans and produces were sub-millisecond while the flag was already being served.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own span-status error signal rose sharply: the 8-minute increase of `traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}` was 0 at 06:01, ~2.1 per 8 min through 06:15-06:24, then 27.7 at 06:26, 99.2 at 06:30 and 163.2 at 06:35; STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET are the only status_code values its series carry.

Latency regression with a comparable baseline: the number of frontend-proxy `ingress` spans longer than 10 s was exactly 0 in every 5-minute window from 06:06:00 through 06:24:00, then 13.3 (window ending 06:25:00), 36.7 (06:26), 73.3 (06:27), 145.6 (06:29) and 126.6-176.7 per 5-minute window for windows ending 06:32-06:38.

The frontend-proxy error spans are HTTP 504 gateway timeouts of ~15.0 s: a read slice of 40 error spans shows `ingress` spans with status tags error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code="ERROR" and duration_us ~15,001,000, each with a child `router frontend egress` span to frontend of ~15.0 s carrying error="true" and http.status_code="0" (no response received).

One whole trace (trace_id d3066bd6d4294c09a9c14e1f7b11fd20, ~06:34:24) shows the request path behind a 504: load-generator POST 15.00 s ending 504 -> frontend-proxy `ingress` 15.00 s ending 504 -> frontend `POST /api/checkout` 15.72 s and `executing api route (pages) /api/checkout` 15.72 s (both http.status_code 200) -> frontend client `grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` 15.72 s -> checkout server `oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` 15.72 s -> checkout `orders publish` 15.58 s; the other downstream calls in the same trace were fast (payment `charge` 34 ms, shipping `/get-quote` 84 ms, cart `GetCart` 1 ms).

checkout's own `orders publish` spans errored during the transition with exact diagnostics: `otel.status_description="kafka: client has run out of available brokers to talk to: dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092: connect: connection refused"` and `otel.status_description="circuit breaker is open"`, with span durations of 27-30 s at 06:24:35-06:25:14; the Service `kafka` in otel-demo has ClusterIP 100.65.62.181 port 9092, i.e. the refused address is the kafka ClusterIP.

checkout pod logs confirm the broker outage window: `Failed to connect to broker kafka:9092: dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092: connect: connection refused` and `Failed to write message: ... circuit breaker is open` repeat from 06:24:21 to 06:25:17, then at 06:25:20.74 `Connected to broker at kafka:9092 (unregistered)` / `Completed ApiVersions request to kafka:9092` / `client/brokers registered new broker #1 at kafka:9092`.

The kafka Deployment was rolled out at 06:23:35: its pod template carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T06:23:35Z, and otel-demo events show Deployment kafka `ScalingReplicaSet` 'Scaled up replica set kafka-5c9d7cc485 from 0 to 1' (06:23:35), ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 `SuccessfulCreate` creating pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 (06:23:35), that pod `Started` (06:23:36), Pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 `Killing` (06:23:37) and Deployment kafka 'Scaled down replica set kafka-ff7884766 from 1 to 0' (06:23:37).

Checkout's Kafka produce latency changed by three orders of magnitude across that rollout: log lines `Successful to write message ... duration: 174.841µs`, `157.19µs`, `134.598µs`, `532.547µs` up to 06:23:39, versus `17.235109912s`, `16.519100427s`, `14.37101277s`, `13.133345631s`, `11.708262725s` at 06:33:05-06:33:16.

The new kafka pod came up with an empty log directory and only became leader of the orders partition at 06:25:16: its log shows `[Broker id=1] Creating new partition orders-0 with topic id jFTsf7SeQ1qWRVM3q-fI-A.`, `[Partition orders-0 broker=1] Log loaded for partition orders-0 with initial high watermark 0` and `[Broker id=1] Leader orders-0 ... starts at leader epoch 0 from offset 0 ... ISR [1]` at 06:25:16.833, and the kafka Deployment's pod template declares no volumes (no volumeMounts on the kafka container).

The kafka container has no readinessProbe or livenessProbe, so the pod's Ready condition turned True at 06:23:37 while the Kafka broker only finished loading and became leader of orders-0 at 06:25:16, matching the ~100 s window in which checkout was refused. Container resources are requests cpu 100m / memory 300Mi, limits cpu 400m / memory 900Mi.

Kafka was CPU-throttled only while starting: usage peaked at 0.297 cores with a 99.5% CFS-throttled ratio at 06:24:06 and 58.8% at 06:25:06, but from 06:26 onward it ran at ~0.014-0.022 cores with a throttled ratio of only 1.4-1.7%, so CPU starvation does not explain the sustained 11-17 s produces.
checkout's container CPU stayed flat at ~0.003-0.006 cores across 06:07-06:36, so the 15 s publishes are waits rather than local computation.

Kafka's current Service endpoints contain exactly one address, 100.96.4.3 (targetRef pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97) on ports plaintext/9092 and controller/9093, the pod is Running/Ready with restartCount 0, and there are no NetworkPolicies and no ResourceQuotas in the cluster; all 5 nodes report Ready with MemoryPressure=False and DiskPressure=False.

The ConfigMap flagd-config (created 2026-11-17T05:50:30Z) holds flag `kafkaQueueProblems` with state ENABLED, defaultVariant "on" (variants off=0, on=100) and description 'Overloads Kafka queue while simultaneously introducing a consumer side delay leading to a lag spike'; checkout runs with FLAGD_HOST=flagd and FLAGD_PORT=8013, and the flagd pod (container started 05:52:18Z) serves flags from a file copied from that ConfigMap.

The declared consumer-side delay of `kafkaQueueProblems` is not visible: accounting's `orders receive` consumer spans longer than 1 s were 0 in every 5-minute window from 06:06 to 06:38, so no consumer-side span delay was observed; only the receive span rate fell from ~195-235 per 5 min to ~130-180 per 5 min, consistent with fewer orders being produced overall.

frontend, checkout and frontend-proxy pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0, and frontend's own span-status error counts are 0 for `POST /api/checkout`, `executing api route (pages) /api/checkout`, `grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder`, `GET` and `POST` throughout 06:22-06:37; the trace shows frontend answering 200 after 15.72 s, so frontend is slow for this cause but not erroring.

Rejected as the cause of the ongoing timeouts: the `connection refused` to 100.65.62.181:9092 explains only 06:24:20-06:25:17; checkout reconnected successfully at 06:25:20.74, yet 504s, slow frontend-proxy ingress spans and 11-17 s produces continued through 06:38, and the kafka Deployment reports availableReplicas=1/readyReplicas=1 with one healthy endpoint.

Principal hypothesis: the kafka Deployment rollout at 06:23:35 (restartedAt annotation; old broker pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 killed 06:23:37, replacement kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 serving only from ~06:25:16) is where this fault originates. Removing the only broker first produced refused connections and checkout publish errors, and the rebuilt (empty /tmp) broker is followed by 11-17 s produce latency for checkout, which pushes PlaceOrder past frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream timeout and yields the 504s. The specific broker-side reason why Produce latency stays at 11-17 s while the broker is ~idle is not shown by the available evidence.

Remaining candidate (unresolved): the fault-injection flag `kafkaQueueProblems` = on in ConfigMap flagd-config. Its name and value declare a Kafka queue/delay fault and it matches the slow-produce symptom in kind, but it cannot be shown to be the cause here: it was already being served from the flagd pod started 05:52:18 while produces were 120-530 us until 06:23:39, its declared consumer-side delay is absent from accounting spans, and the ConfigMap has no incident-time value history to prove when or whether it changed.

A separate change occurred earlier in the window with its own reason: pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm has restartCount 2 with lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137, with otel-demo events `BackOff` at 06:16:41 and `Started` at 06:16:54. Its own span error metric (fraud-detection `flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt`) reads 0 across 06:22-06:38, and no evidence ties it to the frontend-proxy 504s.

Human follow-up on the root cause: retrieve the rollout/audit record for Deployment kafka (annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T06:23:35Z) and any edit to ConfigMap flagd-config around that time, since the change-history integration is not available here.

Operational improvement indicated by the evidence: the kafka container has no readinessProbe, which is why its Pod reported Ready at 06:23:37 while the broker had not yet loaded partitions and become leader of orders-0 until 06:25:16; adding a broker readiness probe (and considering persistent storage instead of the empty in-pod /tmp log dir) would shrink the window in which the Service routed to a broker that refused connections.

The Prometheus rule named RequestErrorRate was not found — list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no rules — so the alert's exact expression, evaluation window and threshold are unverified; the alert's 'current: 0.4' is consistent with ~24 frontend-proxy ingress errors per minute but was not confirmed against the rule.

Logs of the deleted broker pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 are unavailable, and the current kafka container has no previous instance, so the old broker's state before 06:23:37 could not be inspected.
flagd containers returned no readable log lines (0 lines read), so the flag variants actually served to checkout during the incident, and any configuration reload event, could not be verified.
Node-level disk latency/IOPS metrics are not present among the available metrics, so a storage-side explanation for the slow Kafka appends could not be tested.
Impact on callers beyond the observed load-generator checkout requests (other clients, customer-facing consequences) was not measured and is unverified.

Several queries returned nothing and therefore prove nothing: list_prometheus_rules (rule_name RequestErrorRate), get_metric_names {__name__=~"http_.*",service_name="frontend-proxy"}, get_label_values rpc_method for rpc_service oteldemo.CheckoutService, the span-duration queries using le="10000" (the label value is "10000.0"), get_metric_names {service_name="flagd"}, get_prometheus_target otel-collector, and the flagd pod log query each returned no data; these are recorded as unknowns, not as zero or healthy.
next_steps: Pull the cluster audit/changelog for Deployment kafka (otel-demo) around 06:23:35Z and for ConfigMap flagd-config, to identify the actor and intent of the rollout and any concurrent flag edit.

Collect Kafka broker metrics (Produce request time, request queue time, throttle time, log flush and disk latency) for kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 between 06:25 and 06:38 to explain the 11-17 s produce latency.

Confirm the RequestErrorRate alert rule's expression and evaluation window so the reported ratio can be compared directly with the ~24 ingress errors/minute and ~126-177 slow (>10 s) ingress spans per 5 minutes observed here.

If the kafkaQueueProblems flag is not the intended scenario for this incident, review the flagd-config default and set it off, since an enabled fault-injection flag remains a latent risk even though it did not explain this onset.
